items.text: changed: the heads-up display's close button is a drawn multiply sign (two crossing strokes) instead of a letter.
fixed: tapping a Motion setting no longer jumps the pane's scroll somewhere else; it stays where you are.
fixed: holding the crossfader motion button in the Mixer now takes you to the Motion section itself (flashing it), not just to the top of Lines and auto dice.

Motion in the Auto panel (Lines and auto dice, at the bottom). Set how the A|B crossfader moves: shape (sine, triangle, square, saw, smooth random, steps), length counted in beats, bars or minutes, how far it swings, and whether it loops or runs once and holds. Beats and bars follow the tempo while it plays, so a 16-bar swell stays in time at any BPM. Presets: Tide, Breath, Slow Seesaw, Phrase, Section and Rise (32 bars, once).
changed: the crossfader's motion button in the Mixer still taps through the presets; hold it to jump to the Motion settings.
fixed: on a phone the pane's name in the Form panel was cut off ("Lines and auto dic"). The name now gets the room it needs and the hint beside it gives way.

slow motion for the A|B crossfader. A new button beside the crossfader's mode button cycles Off, Tide (a 90-second swell), Breath (12 seconds, small) and Slow Seesaw (a minute from one side to the other). Your hand sets the middle it swings around, so you can still lead, jump and let go. It comes from the same motion kit as Current, so a take will repeat exactly once seeds arrive.

MIDI out. Open the MIDI pane and switch on "Send notes out": every note the grid plays also goes out as a MIDI note, a channel for each colour (or all on channel 1), drums on channel 10, timed to the sound. Pick the output from the list. Chrome on a Mac or a PC; Safari has no MIDI.

MIDI clock out. Switch on "Clock out" and the tempo goes out as MIDI clock (24 a beat) with Start when the robot starts and Stop when it stops, so a synth, a drum machine or Ableton can follow. Tempo changes and glides carry through. Following an outside clock comes later.

Shuffle plays, in Auto dice. Each roll can now move which rows and columns play, as rhythms instead of dice: Walk (a Euclidean rhythm that turns one step each roll), Breathe (a voice comes or goes), Phase (columns and rows slide together, a diagonal), Dealer (a fresh deal) and Flip (play and no-play swap). Choose x columns, y rows or both, and Locks stay keeps locked and always-on rows and columns where they are. Shuffle now does it once.

Surround, for headsets such as Apple Vision Pro: the grid and field on a curved wall all around you, and a pinch works as a touch. The button appears in the bar only where the browser offers it. The room does not show through: Safari on Vision Pro does not allow that to web pages, so it replaces the room. Not yet tried on a headset.
